intro_html: Butter chicken is rich, golden, and downright luxurious, yet this batch clocks in at about $5.07 a bowl (at everyday cost). It is creamy, high in protein, and a rich one to keep in the rotation. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $5.07 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings lands around 57g protein for about 592 calories, at roughly $2.00 a bowl.
upsell_html: Rich and restaurant-worthy, this one will spoil you in the best way. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Stir in Greek yogurt and milk instead of heavy cream to get the richness for a lower cost.
You only need a little butter for the flavor, so one box lasts across several batches.
Buy the chicken breast in bulk and you keep the cost per bowl down.
make_it: Add the chicken breast, chopped onion, and minced garlic to the crock.
Pour in both cans of tomato sauce and drop in the butter with a drizzle of olive oil.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken, then stir in the milk and Greek yogurt for that creamy finish.
Cook the rice while the sauce warms through.
Spoon the butter chicken over rice and serve.

head.description: A high-protein Indian meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 592 calories and 57 grams of protein for roughly $5.07 each (at everyday cost).
